To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the magnetoresistance in multilayer structures with antiferro-magnetic interlayer exchange is enhanced by a factor of 2–5 compared to the usual anisotropie magnetoresistance.
the magnetization of a multilayered magnetic structure can be manipulated by an electrical current and, conversely, that a magnetic field can be used to control a current.

the electrical resistivity of magnetic multilayers with antiferromagnetically coupled layers increases when the magnetic moments of the layers are aligned antiparrallel, and the effect is stronger than the usual magnetoresistance and increases with the number of antiferromagneticaly coupled layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of magnetism in thin films and multilayers.
the magnetoresistance (MR) in layered magnetic structures.
the electrical transport properties of magnetic multilayers and the effect of antiferromagnetic exchange on the magnetoresistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetic anisotropic magnetore-sistance effect is a consequence of the anisotropic scattering of the conduction electrons by the magnetically ordered atoms in the ferromagnets.
the effect of antiferromagnetically coupled layers is to reduce the spin dependent scattering and thus to reduce the magnetoresistance.

the observed magnetoresistance in the Fe Cr Fe structures is due to spin flip scattering of the conduction electrons caused in the ferromagnetic layers by antiparallel alignment with the interlayer magnetization.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spin flip scattering of electrons by the antiferromagnetic exchange interaction is the key to understand this phenomenon.
the antiparallel coupling of the magnetic layers leads to an enhancement of the electrical resistivity.
the magnetoresistive effect is a consequence of the spin dependent scattering of conduction elec trons by magnetic impurities.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the interlayer exchange can be used as a means to manipulate the electrical resistivity of magnetic multilayers.
the interlayer exchange interaction can be controlled by the external magnetic field and can be used to tune the magnetoresistance.
the antiferromagnetic exchange interaction in magnetic multilayers can be used to enhance the magnetoresistance effect, and thus may lead to a new class of spintronic devices.
